targets.notes: Rejection sampling for a domain with a hole walks every candidate row in Python. On 800 points in the unit square minus an overlapping rectangle, cProfile records 1.29 million calls and 0.75s, and the per-coordinate check in CartesianDomain.is_inside accounts for about 0.53s of that. Each kept or rejected row is reshaped into its own LabelTensor, labelled, and passed to is_inside, which calls LabelTensor.extract once per axis. At 2500 points the same call takes about 1.10s, roughly 0.44ms per point, and the cost scales linearly. A mask over the whole batch, using the same comparisons and the same prefix of accepted rows, returns the same coordinates and labels. The number of points drawn from the outer domain stays the same, so the torch random stream stays the same. This is separate from the merged LabelTensor.extract and fast_grad changes: those still run once per row here. It is also separate from boolean LabelTensor indexing, because this sampler never builds a mask.

Exclusion keeps points that lie in exactly one geometry. The sampler splits the request across geometries with random.sample, then for each geometry draws batches and filters them one row at a time. On 400 points from two overlapping rectangles the profile is the same shape as Difference.sample: about 0.59s and 1.11 million calls, mostly LabelTensor.extract inside CartesianDomain.is_inside. At 1500 points the call takes about 1.10s. The row loop calls is_inside, which stacks one boolean per geometry and keeps the row only when the sum is 1. Applying that test to the whole batch, and keeping the same per-geometry quota and the same shuffle, returns the same points and labels. random.sample still decides the geometry order, and each batch is still sized from how many points were accepted, so both random streams stay aligned.

Intersection sampling uses the same per-row rejection loop as Exclusion.sample, with a different keep rule: a row is kept only when it is inside every geometry. On 400 points the profile shows about 0.33s and 620 thousand calls, again dominated by per-row extract inside is_inside. At 2000 points from two overlapping rectangles the call takes about 0.69s. A batch mask that requires every geometry's comparison to pass, then takes the same prefix of accepted rows for each geometry quota, matches the current coordinates and labels. The geometry shuffle and the batch sizes stay the same.
